Nina (Product Design): Quick usability check on the batch vectors preview — two things stood out: the export button visually jumps when you expand rows, and compact rows currently hide the mini-preview users say they rely on. Figma: https://redwood.ai/s/fig-vec-compact :mag:
Ravi (Frontend): I saw the jump too. It's `transform` on .export-toolbar in the expanded state causing relayout. We can reserve the toolbar space (sticky) or anchor the dropdown so it doesn't push. For compact mode, instead of removing previews entirely we could show a 24x24 sparkline micro-graph. Low cost to render as an SVG background.
Jo (Accessibility): Important accessibility notes: export controls need clear aria-labels (e.g., `Export selected vectors`) and keyboard operability (Enter/Space). Row toggles require `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. If we add sparklines, give them `<title>`/`<desc>` or `aria-hidden="false"` with the textual summary for screen readers.
Eli (PM): From research session: "I scan the tiny previews to decide what to open" — so default compact should include a tiny preview. Also users were confused whether Export applied to selected rows or all visible rows. Propose dropdown options: `Export selected`, `Export visible`, `Export all` with helper copy underneath.
Kai (Design): Mocked an alternate toolbar layout: left = compact / comfortable toggle, center = selection count, right = export dropdown (fixed width so it doesn't resize). Tone down the relevance chip contrast and add a subtle border to maintain scanability. Uploaded PNG: https://redwood.ai/s/mock-vec-ctrl.png :art:
Ravi (Frontend): CSS idea (quick):
```css
.row--compact .mini-spark { width: 24px; height: 24px; display:inline-block; background-size: contain; }
.export-dropdown { position: absolute; right: 0; min-width: 220px; }
.toolbar { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 30; }
```
Anchoring the dropdown avoids layout shifts when rows expand. I can prototype in storybook.
Jo (Accessibility): Also consider non-color indicators for relevance mini-previews (bars vs dots). For colorblind users, use bar orientation or fill pattern. Keyboard shortcut request: `e` to open Export when table focus is inside (documented in tooltip). We'll run NVDA pass after prototype.
Eli (PM): Small copy changes: export options should include context line: `Export visible (exports vectors currently in view)` — translations note. Also confirm default compact/comfortable = comfortable for new users; remember preference for signed-in accounts.
Ravi (Frontend): I'll persist preference to localStorage immediately and add an API flag for server-side persistence later. Branch: `design/vector-compact-export`. Will wire storybook knobs: compact/comfortable, sparklines on/off, exportScope. ETA: tomorrow AM.
ci-bot: Preview available: https://staging.redwood.ai/builds/1967890123-storybook (includes storybook entries and export dropdown mock).
Nina (Product Design): Nice. Checklist before PR: update copy for export options, aria-labels on all controls, focus management when dropdown/modal opens (trap focus), compact default=comfortable, add 24px mini-spark for compact rows, and add icon assets for micro-bars. Kai can you add the glyphs to the icon library?
Kai (Design): Adding micro-bar glyphs to `icons-v2`. I'll drop a tiny sprite + SVGs in the design system file by EOD. :white_check_mark:
Ravi (Frontend): Thanks — I'll include the icons and run axe checks in CI. Will ping for a quick a11y walkthrough after PR up.
Nina (Product Design): Thanks team. We'll ship behind `vec-compact-experiment` flag and flip on after a small pilot. Follow-up tomorrow morning to sync on translation strings and analytics events for export counts. :rocket:
